answer: Neighborhood Oasis Rule: each agent must hold a routing position whose immediate peers are mutually connected at a minimum edge density. Enforcement counts unique reciprocal links within two hops; clusters that are isolated islands (no shared neighbors) are rejected as hollow. Registration costs one copper per distinct peer link that must be independently verified by latency handshake, so a sybil ring of N identities needs roughly N² genuine connections. An attacker therefore pays quadratically in bandwidth and coordination, not in tokens.
